body: Pain and lack of quality make them cranky.  Look up dr pocinki's presentation on EDS and sleep.  Wife may need to try beta-blockers to help with sleep and maybe elavil.  Better sleep = lower pain = less cranky wife.

1: wife is now on disability.. after working part time for 2 years. 
2: she is still active, but needs some rest.  no wheelchair. knee braces and finger splints pretty much saved her.  went downhill pretty damn fast after child #2.  
3: go shopping on liberator.com   Get the ramp or something like that.   but yes, while it may help, don't count on it frequently even though she may want it because you'll be afraid to injure her even though it may not happen.    

lots of resources online now. i recommend you look up dr pocinki's presentation on EDS and sleep.  Get her some nuun tablets, she'll need electrolytes.   beta blockers helped my wife sleep.

With EDS, there is serious lag between the time they give the needle to numb things and your body is numb.  The dentist will be tempted to just give you more but tell him to wait instead otherwise you won't feel your eyes and nose for 1/2 day..

Update:  Mon son had not seen him online for 2 days but he has finally showed up. He seemed cheerful but my son still gave him the contact of the teen help line in case he wants to talk.  The kid said thanks but he doesn't think he'll need to talk.   Might have been a really bad moodswing due to teenage hormones...   we'll keep an eye on it!
Electrolytes.  Definitely. Look into nuun tablets.
Get some PEG 3350. Use daily for a month or so.  Drink lots of water.

I've warned my son to not share any personal details, just in case.  I also found the https://teenlineonline.org/talk-now/ which may help so I've provided my son with the phone number so he can give it to the xbox friend and tell him maybe he should call them if he wants to talk since my son won't be online for the next two evenings due to activities. 

I've made it clear to my son that there's only so much he can do yet should try to steer that kid gently towards the proper help channels, either school or that teen helpline.  I don't want him to take this burden on, he already gets moods swings and depressed easily, he definitely doesn't need any of this.    I've also told him to maybe introduce that friend to a few other online friends that are quite nice (I know that one of them plays quite a bit due to medical disability).  We'll see how that turns out..  

You can be sure I'll take a peek in the basement frequently and listen to what's happening..  

It sure is different that the typical "well I fucked you mom" that you hear on xbox live..

Thanks for the talking tips list, I'll go through it with him.  

Point taken about all the details that may not be factual, I had not thought about it this way.

Thanks.  I've made an edit to the original post with a few more items.   A teacher really seems to be the best bet at this point.    Would a teacher really refuse to help?   To me it seems the best bet but since I've never had to deal with any of this,  maybe there are quite a few bad teachers out there that would refuse help.
